DMG_p12.heading: PLAYER CHARACTER NON-PROFESSIONAL SKILLS; separate SECONDARY SKILLS TABLE.
assignment_and_use: The class is treated as the character’s previous primary profession; minor mundane knowledge may derive from earlier years or incidental apprenticeship.
If secondary skills are used in the campaign, the page allows assignment to player characters and optionally henchmen.
The DM may select to fit background or assign randomly from the percentile table.
Prose separately says to roll to determine whether a second skill is known and, on a TWO SKILLS result, assign a second appropriate skill.
The table’s 86–00 result says to roll twice and ignore that result thereafter. The page does not explicitly equate that wording with the prose phrase; keep them distinct.

The DM creates/adjudicates circumstances of use. Examples: judging general worth/soundness, finding food, small repairs, crude construction; an armorer could judge normal armor quality, repair chain links, and perhaps fashion certain weapons.
To gauge extent, consider what a person who knows a little about the subject could do and use that as a relative scale.

rows: Roll twice ignoring this result hereafter
table.coverage: The printed percentile bands span 01–00 (100) without a visible gap or overlap.

system_scope.direct_observation: This page gives an optional assignment table and DM-adjudicated limited background-knowledge examples. It contains no general nonweapon proficiency catalogue, rank progression, check formula, or universal skill-resolution procedure.
system_scope.bounded_classification: Page-specific secondary/background skills; not evidence on its own of a universal nonweapon proficiency subsystem.
system_scope.editorial_caution: Any sentence saying the page does not provide a universal proficiency-check system is an interpretation of this page, not source wording.

UA_Barbarian_pp19_20.category_terms: The UA text calls these primary abilities, secondary abilities, and tertiary skills.

secondary_abilities.name: Survival
secondary_abilities.source_scope: Wild survival: hunting, small-animal trapping, food gathering, shelter/body covering, and fire building.

secondary_abilities.name: First aid
secondary_abilities.source_scope: For the Barbarian: bind wounds, set sprains/broken bones, make natural antidotes/cures; immediately regain 1 hp, then recover at twice the normal rate (2 hp/day resting; 1 hp/day active/adventuring). For others, binding prevents further hp loss; the page says this aid restores 1 hp and increases recovery by 100% if continued aid/cures are administered. Natural poison/illness cure chance is 10%; if the cause is known, the chance is 50 plus the victim’s Constitution score.

secondary_abilities.name: Outdoor craft
secondary_abilities.source_scope: Plant/animal detection as a 3rd-level druid ability, direction finding, and weather prediction as if the same-named spell were cast by a 3rd-level druid.

secondary_abilities.name: Tracking
secondary_abilities.source_scope: Equal to a ranger of the same level, but the Barbarian may track only outdoors.

tertiary_selection_and_native_territory: Every Barbarian possesses all four secondary abilities.

Secondary abilities are generally unusable, certainly not at full potential, in unfamiliar areas. A new locale with different flora, fauna, and climate becomes usable after about one month of continual exposure.
A Barbarian has one or more listed tertiary skills depending on locale/culture; the DM determines which options apply according to the campaign.
Native territory matters: a Barbarian must come from an out-of-the-way barbaric state/area in the campaign; the page gives cavemen, dervishes, nomads, and tribesmen as examples.
Native area informs initial weapons and serves as the basis for judging secondary abilities. Those abilities are severely limited outside the native territory until familiarity increases.
The page supplies Greyhawk cultural/regional examples for Frost/Ice/Snow/Stonefist, Rovers and other nomad groups, and Amedio/Hepmonaland; examples tie culture to selected tertiary skills.

tertiary_options.name: Animal handling
tertiary_options.source_scope: Handle/domesticate wild animals, usually dogs and possibly wolves, large birds, giant lynxes, etc.

tertiary_options.name: Horsemanship
tertiary_options.source_scope: Use a horse in combat; may include handling draft teams.

tertiary_options.name: Long distance signalling
tertiary_options.source_scope: Native signaling methods such as drums, smoke, or mirror flashes for long-distance communication.

tertiary_options.name: Running
tertiary_options.source_scope: Full speed (twice normal movement) for at least three full days, then a day moving at normal rate as rest; endurance is twice normal for movement situations.

tertiary_options.name: Small craft, paddled
tertiary_options.source_scope: Build and use small canoes and hide boats.

tertiary_options.name: Small craft, rowed
tertiary_options.source_scope: Build wooden boats and row and/or sail them.

tertiary_options.name: Sound imitation
tertiary_options.source_scope: Mimic bird/animal calls to lure creatures or signal.

tertiary_options.name: Snare building
tertiary_options.source_scope: Construct deadfalls, pits, and other traps for large and very large animals/creatures.

system_scope.direct_observation: These options and secondary abilities are described for the Barbarian subclass, tied to its class features and DM-selected locale/culture.
system_scope.bounded_classification: Class-specific abilities/skills; these pages do not define a universal nonweapon proficiency list or shared general check procedure.
